    This class also provides additional fields and methods for implementing concrete calendar systems outside the package. These fields and methods are defined asprotected 。

    Like other locale-sensitive classes,CalendarProvides a class methodgetInstance, for getting a generally useful object of this type. CalendarofgetInstancemethod returns aCalendarAn object whose calendar fields have been initialized with the current date and time: 

         Calendar rightNow = Calendar.getInstance();

    CalendarThe object can generate all calendar field values needed to implement date-time formatting for a particular language and calendar style (for example, Japanese - Gregorian, Japanese - Traditional). CalendarDefines the value ranges returned by certain calendar fields and their meanings. For example, the value of the first month of the calendar system for all calendars isMONTH == JANUARY 。 Other values are defined by concrete subclasses, e.g.ERA 。 For more information, please refer to the documentation for each field and the subclass documentation.

    CalendarHas explanation of calendar fields,Loose ， Stricttwo modes. WhenCalendarIn lenient mode, it accepts a wider range of calendar field values than it produces. WhenCalendarrecompute and returnCalendarWhen the calendar field value,get()All calendar fields are normalized. For example, lenientGregorianCalendarExplanationMONTH == JANUARY ， DAY_OF_MONTH == 32such as February 1.

    WhenCalendarWhen in non-lenient mode, if there is any inconsistency in its calendar fields, an exception is thrown. For example,GregorianCalendarAlways generates a value between 1 and the length of the monthDAY_OF_MONTHvalue. If any field value has been set out of range, then non-lenientGregorianCalendarThrows an exception when calculating its time or calendar field values.

    First Week

    CalendarDefines a locale-specific seven-day work week using two parameters: the first day of the week and the minimum number of days in the first week (from 1 to 7). When constructingCalendarWhen, these numbers are taken from the locale resource data or the locale itself. If the specified locale contains 'fw' and/or 'rg'Unicode extensions, then the first day of the week is obtained according to these extensions. If both 'fw' and 'rg' are specified, the values in the 'fw' extension will override the implied values in the 'rg' extension. They can also be explicitly specified by methods that set their values.

    Calendar field resolution

    fromCalendarFieldsComputedayperiodandTimewhen,possibleno足够ofInformationused forCompute（For exampleOnlyyearmonthandmonth份nodayperiod）, orpossibleExistsNoconsistentofInformation（For example1996year7month15day星period二（格里High利） ） - 1996year7month15dayreal际TopYes星periodone）。 CalendarThe calendar field values will be parsed to determine the date and time as follows.

    If there is any conflict in calendar field values, Calendar gives priorities to calendar fields that have been set more recently.The following are the default combinations of calendar fields. The latest combination determined by the most recently set single field will be used.

    For the date fields ： 

     YEAR + MONTH + DAY_OF_MONTH
 YEAR + MONTH + WEEK_OF_MONTH + DAY_OF_WEEK
 YEAR + MONTH + DAY_OF_WEEK_IN_MONTH + DAY_OF_WEEK
 YEAR + DAY_OF_YEAR
 YEAR + DAY_OF_WEEK + WEEK_OF_YEAR
    For the time of day fields ： 
     HOUR_OF_DAY
 AM_PM + HOUR

    If any calendar field value is not set in the selected field combination, thenCalendarWill use its default value. The default value of each field may vary depending on the specific calendar system. For example, inGregorianCalendar, the default value of a field is the beginning of the same era: that is,YEAR = 1970 ， MONTH = JANUARY ， DAY_OF_MONTH = 1, etc.

    Note:There are some possible ambiguities in the interpretation of certain singular times, which can be resolved by the following means:

    1. 23:59 is the last minute of the day, and 00:00 is the first minute of the next day. Therefore, 23:59 on December 31, 1999 < 00:00 on January 1, 2000 < 00:01 on January 1, 2000.
    2. Although历史TopNo准confirm，午夜alsoAttributein“Top午”，Medium午Attributein“Bottom午”, so insameone天，凌晨12:00（午夜）<12:01 am，Medium午12:00（Medium午）<12 ：01 pm

    : The calendar fields can be changed in three waysset() ， add()androll() 。

    set(f, value)Change calendar fieldsfTovalue 。 In addition, it sets internal member variables to indicate calendar fields.fChanged. Therefore, forset()Multiple calls will not trigger multiple unnecessary computations. as usedset()As a result of changing a calendar field, other calendar fields may also change, depending on the calendar field, the calendar field value, and the calendar system.     For example: considerGregorianCalendarInitially set to 1999, called August 31,set(Calendar.MONTH, Calendar.SEPTEMBER)Set date to September 31, 1999, this is a temporary internal representation parsed as October 1, 1999, ifgetTime(), then call. However, when callingset(Calendar.DAY_OF_MONTH, 30)called beforegetTime()Set the date to September 30, 1999, because inset()Not recalculated afterwards.

    add(f, delta)IncreasedeltaOn sitef 。 This is equivalent to calling adjust twice.set(f, get(f) + delta) ：

    Add rule 1. The value of field f after the call minus the value of field f before the call is delta, modulo any overflow that has occurred in field f. Overflow occurs when a field value exceeds its range and, as a result, the next larger field is incremented or decremented and the field value is adjusted back into its range.

    Add rule 2. If a smaller field is expected to be invariant, but it is impossible for it to be equal to its prior value because of changes in its minimum or maximum after field f is changed or other constraints, such as time zone offset changes, then its value is adjusted to be as close as possible to its expected value. A smaller field represents a smaller unit of time. HOUR is a smaller field than DAY_OF_MONTH. No adjustment is made to smaller fields that are not expected to be invariant. The calendar system determines what fields are expected to be invariant.

    In addition, withset()Different,add()Force an immediate recalculation of the calendar's millisecond value and all fields.

    For example: considerGregorianCalendarInitially set to 1999, called August 31,add(Calendar.MONTH, 13)Set the calendar to September 30, 2000.Add rule 1setMONTHField to September, because adding 13 months to the month gives next year's September. Due toDAY_OF_MONTHcannot be in SeptemberGregorianCalendar, thereforeAdd rule 2willDAY_OF_MONTHSet to the nearest possible value. Although it is a smaller field,DAY_OF_WEEKRule 2 does not apply toDAY_OF_WEEKAn adjustment is made because when the month is inGregorianCalendarWhen a change occurs, it is expected to change.

    roll(f, delta)IncreasedeltaOn sitefDoes not change larger fields. This is equivalent to calling with the following adjustmentsadd(f, delta) ：

    Roll rule. Larger fields are unchanged after the call. A larger field represents a larger unit of time. DAY_OF_MONTH is a larger field than HOUR.

    Example: seeGregorianCalendar.roll(int, int) 。

        public static final int DAY_OF_WEEK_IN_MONTH
        getandsetField number indicating the ordinal number of the day of the week within the current month. andDAY_OF_WEEKFields together uniquely specify a day within a month. UnlikeWEEK_OF_MONTHandWEEK_OF_YEAR, the value of this fieldNotDepends ongetFirstDayOfWeek()orgetMinimalDaysInFirstWeek() 。 DAY_OF_MONTH 1To7always correspondsDAY_OF_WEEK_IN_MONTH 1 ; 8to14corresponds toDAY_OF_WEEK_IN_MONTH 2, and so on. DAY_OF_WEEK_IN_MONTH 0RepresentsDAY_OF_WEEK_IN_MONTH 1the previous week. Negative values are counted from the end of the month; therefore, the last Sunday of a month is specified asDAY_OF_WEEK = SUNDAY, DAY_OF_WEEK_IN_MONTH = -1 。 Since negative values count backward, they are usually aligned differently within the month than positive values. For example, if a month has 31 days, thenDAY_OF_WEEK_IN_MONTH -1will overlapDAY_OF_WEEK_IN_MONTH 5and4end.

      • roll

        public abstract void roll​(int field,
                          boolean up)
        Add or subtract (up/down) a single unit of time on a given time field without changing larger fields. For example, to move the current date one day earlier, you can achieve it by calling:

        roll（Calendar.DATE，true）。 When rolling on the year or Calendar.YEAR field, it will roll the year value, ranging between 1 and by callinggetMaximum(Calendar.YEAR)between the returned values. When rolling on the month or Calendar.MONTH field, other fields (such as date) may conflict and need to be changed. For example, rolling the month on the date 01/31/96 will result in 02/29/96. When rolling on the hour or Calendar.HOUR_OF_DAY field, it will roll the hour value within the range from 0 to 23, starting at zero.

        Parameter
        field- the time field.
        up- Indicates whether to add or roll the value of the specified time field. Use true if scrolling, otherwise use false.
        See also:
        add(int,int) ， set(int,int)
